arabic_locator.text: [كُلُّ هَذِهِ الْأَقْوَالِ غَرِيبَةٌ جِدًّا]  وَالصَّحِيحُ الْقَوْلُ الْأَوَّلُ، أَنَّ الْمُرَادَ بِالنَّحْرِ ذَبْحُ الْمَنَاسِكِ؛

semantic_units.statement_en: The captured Arabic text includes a bracketed assessment that all these interpretations are very unusual.
Ibn Kathir identifies the first interpretation as correct: nahr means slaughtering sacrificial animals.

fidelity_notes: Preserve square brackets exactly; their presence alone does not establish manuscript or editorial provenance.
Separate the bracketed collective assessment from the unbracketed preference statement.
Do not convert gharib jiddan concerning interpretations into a technical hadith grading of every preceding report.
Correct marks the author's interpretive preference, not independent verification.
Analytical English paraphrase; corresponding bounded English transition omits this unit.
disagreement: The preferred sacrificial-slaughter reading differs from the preceding hand-placement, hand-raising, qibla-facing and post-bowing posture interpretations.
remaining: Verify exact context and separate clause locators against captured witness
